summary: Check of test artifacts only (no browser/API/DB re-run, as requested). /app/tests/pos_attendance_regression_iter52.py and iter53.py were converted from top-level tool snippets into valid importable modules with `async def run(page)`. The body was wrapped mechanically with 4-space indentation, and every assertion and the rest of the flow is unchanged (a whitespace-insensitive diff shows only the wrapper and fail-fast lines). Fail-fast: in the except block, the exception screenshot is wrapped in its own try so it can't hide the original error, then the exception is re-raised with `raise`. After SUMMARY, the script raises AssertionError if any rec() is FAIL or if there are no results. URL comes from frontend/.env and credentials from /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Both are read inside run(), so importing the module has no side effects, and no credentials are printed. Checks: py_compile OK for both files; `ruff --select F704,F821` and `ruff --select F,E9` both pass with 0 errors (previously 99); pyflakes clean (I removed the unused asyncio import in iter53); importlib loads both, and run is a coroutine function with signature (page). Fail-fast smoke test with a fake page that throws: exceptions propagated correctly from both modules. The app was not changed.
critical_code_review_comments: The strict ruff ruleset (plugin default) still reports non-error style findings: I001 (import order), SIM115/ASYNC230 (open() without a context manager inside async; mostly already in the original code), FURB167 (re.M), S110/BLE001 (try-except-pass around the exception screenshot, which is deliberate so the original error is kept). There are no F-class/syntax errors. These are optional to tidy up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: How to run: in Playwright async code, `import importlib.util as u; s=u.spec_from_file_location('m','/app/tests/pos_attendance_regression_iter53.py'); m=u.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m); await m.run(page)`. In the browser_automation tool you can also paste the file contents and add `await run(page)` at the end. run() raises AssertionError when an assertion fails and re-raises exceptions. iter52 still saves screenshots to .screenshots/ as in the original flow (the folder is created automatically). Last functional results: 46/46 (iter52) and 28/28 (iter53 retest).
